facts.F1: Follow-up to nav-collapse-toggle (EXAMINE accepted at 60a4e36). The user decided: (1) Sign out stays in the collapsed strip; (2) fix all five non-blocking findings of the nav-collapse-toggle whole-candidate review; (3) the collapsed left nav shows icons instead of hiding its links. The five findings: [oracle] feature_canzan_theme.rs neighbour arm weakened to deferred_neighbours > 0 — assert every non-pre-paint head script defers; [oracle] its panic text says theme.js is the ONE pre-paint script and its doc says five neighbouring tags (there are two pre-paint and seven deferred); [oracle] fn head_scripts duplicated in feature_nav_collapse.rs, feature_canzan_theme.rs and xtask — one shared owner under crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/; [implementation] xtask check_arch pre-paint set decided by narrow substrings — widen to names localStorage/sessionStorage AND names documentElement; [implementation] base.html comments say the deferred five, the head declares seven. Second-tab sync stays out of scope.
facts.F10: the board opens, the left nav is still collapsed, and the Board icon is marked as the page she is on
facts.F100: The collapsed geometry exists only where scripting ran: nothing but static/js/nav-collapse.js stamps the marker. So every promise of the collapsed rail is a promise about a scripting-on document, and the scripting-off document is the expanded text nav it is today. This is a bound on the promise, not a deviation from it.
facts.F101: Test-time: both slices work inside the project default budgets, so no derogation is requested and none is granted. S1 lands in the default suite through cargo xtask smoke, where the gate rule and its staged-tree fixtures are straight-line file reads. S2 scenarios are @needs-browser and therefore excluded from the default fast lane; they run in cargo xtask ci only with FOUNDRY_XTASK_INCLUDE_DOCKER=1, which every verification command for S2 names. A Docker-less gate observes NOTHING of S2.
facts.F102: Checker environment: Quint 0.32.0 with the Apalache backend in the shared Lima VM local-dev, reached through scripts/test-in-lima.sh and run from a scratch copy outside the repository.
